title: Validation of<input> type='date' not conforming to ISO 8601-2

labels.name: needs implementer interest
labels.description: Moving the issue forward requires implementers to express interest

labels.name: i18n-tracker
labels.description: Group bringing to attention of Internationalization, or tracked by i18n but not needing response.

body:
Opened by @akehir as w3c/html#1340. It seems like a good use case, so opening here for discussion with implementors.

># Introduction
While implementing a form recording birth dates as written on official passports and similar travel documents, I've stumbled on a small issue with the <input> type='date'.

# Background
The underlying issue is, that the Swiss Government may issue identity cards or passports which do include a birth day of '00' and a birth month of '00', as it has happened with [this example](https://www.swissinfo.ch/eng/red-tape-quirk_when-your-birthdate-lands-you-in-trouble/44023072). The official birth date is actually specified as **00 00 68** on the passport. According to the officials, this practise is based on the [following law](https://www.admin.ch/opc/de/classified-compilation/20092157/index.html#a6),  which was written in conformance to the guidelines of the  International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) on Machine Readable Travel Documents. The 7th edition from 2015 is retrievable as [PDF](https://www.icao.int/publications/Documents/9303_p3_cons_en.pdf).

This document, valid for 191 [member states](https://www.icao.int/about-icao/Council/Pages/council-states-2016-2019.aspx) regulates how birth dates may be recorded. While they do not foresee the '00' used by Switzerland, they write the following:

> Unknown date of birth. Where a date of birth is completely unknown, that data element shall appear in the date format used for dates of birth by the issuing State or organization but with Xs representing unknown elements (numbers and/or letters) of the date.
> 
> Examples:
> XXbXXbXX
> XXbXXbXXXX
> XXbXXXbXX where b = a single blank space.
> 
> If only part of the date of birth is unknown, only that part (day, month, year) of the date shall be represented by Xs as per the date format used by the issuing State or organization

As well as using an empty filler character for the machine readable format:

> If all or part of the date of birth is unknown, the relevant character positions shall be completed with filler characters (<).

# Issues with HTML Specification
The HTML specification uses the ISO 8601 standard (2004), upon which [date validation in general](https://www.w3.org/TR/html5/infrastructure.html#valid-date-string), and the [date input in particular](https://www.w3.org/TR/html5/sec-forms.html#element-statedef-input-date) is based. The current standard does not foresee any 'unknown' dates.

Additionally. the recommendations for [Autofill ](https://www.w3.org/TR/html5/sec-forms.html#autofill-field) for 'bday' as well are also based on the incorrect assumption that birth dates are issued in compliance with the ISO 8601 standard from 2014. The recommendation is to use the date input element, and to only allow valid dates. 

Therefore, people with unknown birth days / months will encounter issues when trying to enter their official birth date anywhere in the web, where a input type date is used. In our case, we'd need to opt for a text input field with a custom validation - in the end this defeats having a standardized input field for dates.

A solution might lie in the forthcoming update to the ISO 8601 standard, which does cover the problematic case of unknown date parts.

# ISO 8601-2 Recognizes 'X' as placeholder for unknown dates
In the [ISO 8601-2 (extensions), 2016](https://www.loc.gov/standards/datetime/iso-tc154-wg5_n0039_iso_wd_8601-2_2016-02-16.pdf) draft standard, the use of an 'X' for an unknown date has been adopted:

> 4.3 Unspecified
> The character 'X'	may be used as a replacement character, in place of a digit to indicate that the value of that digit is unspecified.
> 4.3.1 Level 1
> The replacement character ‘X’ may be substituted for the right-most digits in the following cases:
> • Year and month specified, day unspecified.
> • Year specified, day and month unspecified.
> • Entire date unspecified
> Representations with reduced accuracy
> For representations with reduced accuracy,  ‘X’ may be used in the following cases:
> • A year-month, with month unspecified.
> • A year-month, with year and month unspecified.
> • A year with one or two (rightmost) unspecified digits.
> • A year, entire year unspecified. 
> 4.3.2 Level 2
> For level 2 the character ‘X’ may be used as a replacement for any character in the string. 


# Resolution
Preferably, the HTML specification would also allow for 'X' to be used in birth dates, or dates in general. Unfortunately, this will make date validation more complicated, as more than only numbers would be acceptable.

Maybe, date validation needs to distinguish the exact / inexact case, or the birthday case - although exact dates can easily be implemented with regex patterns.

This would not completely remedy the '00' date as issued by Switzerland, as it's not compliant to the new ISO spec. I do not know how many countries have a similar issuing policy.>
